# Threat model: scan-target.vendetta.lab:8080

## Overview
Intentionally vulnerable Node.js/Express shop used as the authorised lab target of the Vendetta stack. A single-page Angular front end talks to a REST API under /rest and /api backed by an embedded SQLite database. It holds no real customer data; the value at stake is demonstrating detection and response.

## Trust Boundaries and Assumptions
- Internet/lab client -> Express app on :8080 (no WAF, no TLS termination in the lab).
- Express app -> SQLite file on the same host (full read/write by the application account).
- Vendetta agent on the same host watches /var/log and the application directory (FIM) and ships events to the manager.
Assumption: the host is reachable only from the lab network; every request in scope originates from the Errow sandbox.

## Attack Surface and Attacker Stories
- Unauthenticated attacker abuses /rest/products/search?q= to read the Users table (SQL injection).
- A victim opens a crafted /#/search?q= link and the reflected value executes script (XSS).
- Verbose errors on /api/* leak framework versions and filesystem paths, easing follow-on attacks.
User-controlled inputs: query string, JSON bodies, cookies, Authorization header, uploaded file names.

## Severity Calibration
Critical: unauthenticated remote code execution or full credential database disclosure with reusable secrets. High: authenticated-user data disclosure or SQL injection reaching credential tables. Medium: client-side injection requiring victim interaction. Low: information disclosure without direct exploitation path.

amendments.content: Confirmed the SQLite back-end and nine-column product query; the Users table stores MD5 password hashes, which raises the SQL injection impact to credential disclosure.
